_voted_data_note: Chili Tropper left the list on 2026-09-06 (joining Yashar at number six) and Yoaz Hendel immediately joined forces with Prof. Yaron Zelekha's Economic Party. The list therefore has no 25th-Knesset voting data: Hendel was not a 25th-Knesset MK (his 23rd/24th-Knesset record under Blue and White / Derech Eretz aligns with the national_unity data here) and Zelekha has never been an MK.

stated_position.source: Joint 'Magen David' platform (launched 2026-08): within 90 days of forming a government, approve a national programme strengthening Kiryat Shmona, the Galilee, the Negev, the Gaza-envelope communities, the Jordan Valley, Judea and Samaria and the eastern border settlements; HaMiluimnikim settlement initiative continues under the merged list

Hendel characterizes conflict as 'clash of civilizations' where 'peace is unlikely without change that will take generations'; dismissed diplomatic engagement as a mistake that contributed to October 7; shifted rightward post-Oct 7 advocating territorial control in Lebanon and Gaza

Party platform: 'Israel should adopt an aggressive security policy that moves the decision to enemy territory — from containment to initiative and offensiveness'; Hendel supports expanded Israeli presence in Gaza post-conflict and controlling northern Gaza
Hendel stated 'united Jerusalem is our fiction' (ירושלים המאוחדת שלנו היא בדיון); pragmatic-nationalist approach rather than maximalist permanent sovereignty claim
Opposes right of return

Hendel at Herzliya Conference 2013: proposed annexing settlement blocs and the Jordan Valley (granting citizenship to Arab residents); party's settlement initiative actively promotes settlement in Jordan Valley and Gaza Envelope post-war
Hendel's threshold condition for joining any coalition: a conscription law obligating every citizen to serve in the military, national or civil service, passed before the government is formed
Hendel is secular; supports civil marriage
Supports Shabbat commerce freedom
Supports religious pluralism at Western Wall
Hendel ties benefits to service ('no rights without obligations'); public funding for institutions is conditioned on the core curriculum
Zelekha's Economic Party platform calls for opening kashrut certification to competition in order to lower food prices - an anti-monopoly rather than religious-enforcement approach

Zelekha's Economic Party platform: declare exclusive importers monopolies and enforce competition law, abolish import quotas, cut VAT from 18% to 12% and income-tax ceilings to 40%, and move expensive infrastructure projects out of 'cumbersome government companies' into joint management with the private sector

Platform commits to 'strengthening the judiciary while preserving the balance between the branches'; Hendel as an MK opposed the override clause and Tropper opposed the 2023 judicial overhaul as a National Unity MK
Platform frames judicial change as strengthening the courts within a balanced separation of powers, not as political control of appointments
Supports AG authority as rule-of-law safeguard
Supports judicial review including reasonableness standard
Platform: advance a Zionist constitution and strengthen the judiciary while preserving checks and balances between the branches
Supports equality for all citizens who fulfil civic obligations (service)
Hendel sets the formation of a 'Zionist government' as a threshold condition and opposes 'autonomous zones' in Arab-majority and Haredi communities

Platform proposes a dedicated security-agency unit against crime in Arab society and a new public-safety authority, alongside state services in place of 'autonomies' — enforcement and service delivery framing rather than a funding-equality commitment
Neutral on Nation-State Law; not a party focus
Supports PM accountability; part of pro-rule-of-law bloc
Hendel's governance platform proposes limiting the tenure of elected officials
Mid-sized party; would benefit from higher threshold eliminating smaller fringe parties
Hendel built his political comeback around the reserve-officer critique of the 7 October failures and has consistently backed a state commission of inquiry
Public funding exclusively for institutions teaching the core curriculum (math, English, sciences)
Supports professional media standards and preventing systematic disinformation
No public stance on gender parity in electoral lists found
Zelekha's platform mentions environmental protection and water management but commits to no binding climate legislation
